definitions.explanation: The quality of being passed down through genes from parent to offspring. Used in medical, scientific, and everyday contexts when discussing traits or conditions that run in families.

examples.japanese: この{病気|びょうき}には{遺伝性|いでんせい}がある。
examples.english: This disease has a hereditary nature.

examples.japanese: {遺伝性|いでんせい}の{疾患|しっかん}について{医師|いし}に{相談|そうだん}した。
examples.english: I consulted a doctor about hereditary disorders.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}の{病歴|びょうれき}から{遺伝性|いでんせい}のリスクを{調|しら}べることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to examine hereditary risk from family medical history.

notes:
Composed of {遺伝|いでん} (heredity, genetics) and {性|せい} (nature, quality). Functions as a noun and also as a modifier before other nouns using the の particle. Frequently appears in medical and scientific contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遺伝性|いでんせい}の{病気|びょうき}: hereditary disease
- {遺伝性|いでんせい}の{疾患|しっかん}: hereditary disorder
- {遺伝性|いでんせい}がある: to have a hereditary nature
- {遺伝性|いでんせい}が{高|たか}い: to be highly hereditary

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遺伝|いでん}: heredity — the broader concept of genetic inheritance
- {先天性|せんてんせい}: congenital — present from birth, but not necessarily inherited
- {家族性|かぞくせい}: familial — running in families, which may include both genetic and environmental factors
